transcript.text: My Shark cordless battery got really hot on charge last night and this morning it looks puffed up, the plastic case has split at the seam a bit. Can I still use it till a new one comes? It's the IZ201UK.

No, please don't use or charge it again. A lithium-ion battery that overheated, swelled, and split its case has internal damage. It can catch fire or vent toxic smoke, sometimes hours or days later and without warning. This is a real fire risk, not just a performance issue.

What to do now:

1. Unplug the charger and take the battery off the vacuum if it's still attached. Don't force it if it's stuck; if it won't come out easily, put the whole vacuum somewhere safe instead.
2. Move it somewhere it can't start a fire. Outside is best: on a patio, concrete, or bare ground, away from the house, sheds, cars, and anything flammable. A metal bucket or a bed of sand works well. If you can't put it outside, place it on a non-flammable surface away from soft furnishings, and don't leave it in a bedroom or on an escape route.
3. Don't puncture, squash, or try to open it, and don't put it in water, the freezer, or a sealed container.
4. Watch for warning signs: hissing, smoke, a sweet or chemical smell, or further heat or swelling. If it starts smoking or catches fire, get away from it and call 999. Don't try to tackle a lithium battery fire yourself.

Getting rid of it:

• Don't put it in your household bin or recycling. Damaged lithium batteries cause a lot of bin lorry and recycling centre fires in the UK.
• Contact your local council or household recycling centre and tell them it's a damaged/swollen lithium battery. Many have specific arrangements, and some won't accept damaged ones in the normal battery bin.
• Some retailers' battery collection points also won't take damaged packs, so check first.

Contact Shark:

• Report it to Shark UK customer service. A battery overheating and swelling on its own charger is something they'll want to know about, and depending on its age it may be covered under warranty.
• Tell them what happened with the charger too. Stop using the charger until you've spoken to them, in case it contributed.
• It's also worth checking the UK Product Safety recall database (via GOV.UK) for your model.

When you order a replacement, buy a genuine Shark battery or one from a reputable seller. Cheap unbranded packs are a common cause of these failures.

I know it's annoying to be without the vacuum for a few days, but this one really isn't worth the risk.
